text.name: AutoPlay
text.titlePass: AutoPlay is off for all drives
text.why: AutoPlay opens or runs what is on a USB stick or disc as soon as it is plugged in, before you have looked at it.
fix: Open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > AutoPlay and turn AutoPlay off for yourself.
For the whole PC, tell IT: the policy is "Turn off Autoplay", set to All drives.

absent.found: Not configured for the whole PC (Windows default: AutoPlay on)

text.name: AutoRun commands
text.titlePass: Drives cannot start programs by themselves
text.titleFail: Drives can offer to start programs by themselves
text.why: An autorun command on a USB stick or disc names a program to start. Malware on removable drives relies on it.
fix: This is normally set for all PCs at once: tell IT.
The policy is "Set the default behavior for AutoRun", set to "Do not execute any autorun commands".

absent.found: Not configured (Windows default: the user is asked)

text.name: Elevated installs (PC)
text.titlePass: Installers do not get administrator rights by default
text.titleFail: The PC lets installers run with administrator rights
text.why: With this policy on, any user or any malware can install software with full control of the PC by wrapping it in an installer.
fix: Tell IT: the policy "Always install with elevated privileges" must be disabled.
It is set for the PC in the key shown in the details.

text.name: Elevated installs (user)
text.titlePass: Your installers do not get administrator rights by default
text.titleFail: Your account lets installers run with administrator rights
text.why: Together with the same policy for the PC, any program you run can install software with full control of the PC.
fix: Tell IT: the policy "Always install with elevated privileges" must be disabled.
It is set for your account in the key shown in the details.

text.name: Printer driver installs
text.titlePass: Only administrators can install printer drivers
text.why: A printer driver runs deep inside Windows. Letting any user install one was the opening for the PrintNightmare attacks.
fix: Tell IT: the value RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators shown in the details must be 1 or absent.
If printers stop installing afterwards, IT can pre-install their drivers.
